MITCHELL'S FORMAL WEAR.note: Mitchell's Formal Wear: the logo from the ad, black on a white panel: Mitchell's in a heavy calligraphic italic, a rule beneath it broken in the middle by a bow tie, and FORMAL WEAR in widely spaced roman capitals with the registered mark.

SAADI'S.note: Saadi's haberdashery: from the owner's photo of the sign. A black fascia; Saadi's in heavy light-grey serif, and under it to the right a grey box with haberdashery in black bold serif lowercase, a fine grey rule running in from the left to the box's middle and a small tick off its right side.

GADZOOKS.note: Gadzooks: gloss-black square tile with pale grout, a red open-face neon logo with the big linked OO, and red / white / blue neon tubes running out to each side of it

AFTERTHOUGHTS.note: Afterthoughts: mauve mosaic tile, raised pink speed-lines, tall white deco letters with the big round O, and a wide open front onto warm slatwall hung with bags and a spinner of earring cards || Afterthoughts lettering (from the photo): thin white lower-case, round and airy

COUNTY SEAT.note: County Seat: slate-green tile fascia, heavy white rounded capitals with the centre dot, pale block piers, and an open front onto walls of hung sweaters and tables stacked with folded jeans

RADIO SHACK.note: Radio Shack (from the photos): a deep brown fascia box with the lit red wordmark standing off it on dark returns, a bright soffit, and an aluminium-and-glass front on a green marble plinth. The window is dressed the way the photos show: slatwall of carded parts, oak slat fixtures of boxed software, the beige computer with its keyboard and printer on an oak stand, a stereo, and the telephone wall under its hanging sign; the open door shows the aisle running back.

WICKS 'N' STICKS.note: Wicks 'N' Sticks (from the photos): a cedar-board front with a round-shouldered fascia, white rounded letters with an arch and a red flame over each word, a bay window crammed with baskets, baubles and candles on stepped oak tiers, and the open way in showing the long wall of tapers in every colour over a blue carpet.

GENERAL NUTRITION CENTER.note: GNC (from the photo): a portal of honed stone tile with the three red letters standing off the lintel, glass either side on black plinths stacked with tubs, a banner in the window, and the bright shop of shelves beyond.

CHAMPS SPORTS.note: Champs Sports (from the photos): a smooth white portal with the navy badge outlined in red, cream serif capitals and SPORTS in its lower lobe; a royal-blue soffit with downlights; the blue WE KNOW GAME panel on a grey block plinth; a dark ceiling hung with rows of dome pendants, a slat-wood back wall of hung tops, a mannequin in a teal tee and white cap at the glass doors, and a wall of trainers on the right.

B. DALTON BOOKSELLER.note: B. Dalton (from the photos): a deep oxblood fascia box with the flowing white script and its long tail, recessed downlights under it, cream piers banded in brown; inside, shelf on shelf of spines with a face-out row along the top, the red and green seasonal banners with their white moons and silhouettes, a Bestsellers header, a spinner of paperbacks and a table stacked for the front of the shop on a honey wood floor.

SEARS.note: Sears (from the photos): a wall of big buff ceramic tile, a darker grey tile band framing the mouth, SEARS in heavy slanted navy channel letters with a white halo behind them; the mouth wide open on a bright sales floor of columns, racks, red SALE signs, the blue cashback banner, a round blue table, security pedestals and a tall black tower sign.

MERRY-GO-ROUND.note: Merry-Go-Round (from the photos): a gloss-black fascia with fat round tube letters, MERRY red, GO yellow, ROUND green; dark-framed windows either side, and a bright open front: sunset stripes on the wall, the I.O.U. banner hung across, rails of jackets and tops, a round rack of striped shirts out front, a red-skirted table, sale boards on easels, glossy wood.

ATHLETE'S FOOT.note: Athlete's Foot (from the photo): a black fascia hung on rods, yellow round lettering and the red winged foot, between warm timber panels, one carrying a tall landscape poster; inside, the shoe wall, stacks of blue and red boxes, a timber column with the oval badge, the sock wall, a black-draped table of shoes with its SALE card, a red promo stand and a blue notice on an easel, all on a honey timber floor.

ORANGE JULIUS.note: Orange Julius (from the photo): cream tile, a raised sign board with the name in looping orange neon, a course of red tiles set with black diamonds; inside, pale walls hung with a row of framed prints, the tiled counter under black menu light-boxes with the steel of the kitchen behind, oak booths either side, a dark red floor, a queue post, a brick pier.

THE SHOE DEPT.note: The Shoe Dept. (from the photos): a band and piers of pink-grey granite, "the" in white script beside wide-spaced block capitals, brass-framed show windows either side with their posters, and a deep shop of shoe aisles round a curved display.

PAYLESS SHOES.note: Payless ShoeSource (from the photos): a black fascia with fat yellow serif lettering, the two o's as orange discs, downlights under it and yellow columns; a bright shop: slatwall of handbags, the red feature wall on its white steps, aisles of boxed shoes under orange 50% signs, shoe towers at the door and an orange circle let into the dark carpet.

5-7-9.note: 5-7-9 (from the photos): a smooth putty wall with the oval badge, magenta ring, silver field, brushed magenta numerals; a frameless glass front on a bright magenta shop, neon tops along the walls, forms in denim on a white plinth.

KAY-BEE TOYS.note: Kay-Bee Toys (from the photos): white tile flecked with red and blue squares, a royal-blue fascia with lit red slab capitals, an egg-crate ceiling of light, blue columns, a red ball on a blue pedestal; the shop stacked floor to ceiling with boxed toys under yellow and green sale banners, plush along the top shelf, a table of boxes out front.

JW.note: JW (from the photograph): a pale speckled wall; a tall portal with its top corners cut at 45 degrees, drawn as a charcoal outer band and a light grey inner band, both kicking outward at the floor; a charcoal lozenge at the head with the white JW between two thin red rules; and an open front onto a cream shop with a wood floor: folded jeans on shelves at the back, posters above, a round rack of denim shirts in the middle and a mannequin either side. Every edge is square or a true 45-degree cut, so the lines stay clean.

GREAT AMERICAN COOKIE CO.note: Great American Cookie Co. (from the photo): a cream sign box with maroon checkerboard corners, Great American in yellow neon script on a maroon lobe over the black pill of white capitals; under warm downlights a row of back-lit menu pictures, white tile with a red check course, the glass case of cookies, lit panels of cookie cakes and the heart-shaped specials.

CHICK-FIL-A.note: Chick-fil-A (from the photo): a bulkhead of tan tile set on the diagonal, a deep red sign box with the script name in hot pink-white neon, the C wearing its comb and beak; below, the long timber counter with dark inset rounds under a row of back-lit menu boards, steel and tills behind, silver balloons, a dining corner of timber booths and a white draped table.

REGIS HAIRSTYLISTS.note: Regis (from the photos): honed travertine with a black cornice, triple black stripes banding the piers, a black plinth, the name in heavy black letters with light spilling round them; a tall window on the salon floor of black chairs and mirrors, the open reception with its maple desk and portraits, and walls of bottles in every colour.

SPORTS AVENUE.note: Sports Avenue (from the photos): the whole front hangs off a gold goalpost: a red padded post at the door, a goose-neck curving up to the crossbar, uprights rising past the sign with red flags on top. Between the uprights a gold marquee, wider at the top, carries a field of white bulbs with SPORTS picked out in red, a star at each corner; under it AVENUE in separate gold capitals on a rail against blue. Behind the glass: jerseys pinned in a grid, forms in hoods and shorts, caps, a red table.

OPTICAL OUTLET.note: Optical Outlet (from the Southland photo): a ribbed lilac-grey fascia with fat round lower-case letters glowing warm yellow; dark-framed glass and doors on a bright cream shop: walls of frames, lit cases, portraits of faces in glasses.

COACH HOUSE GIFTS.note: Coach House Gifts (from the photo): a course of small black tile, a smooth grey fascia with white serif capitals, black tile piers; a deep shop with sea-green slat walls, hanging banners and a flag, tables and towers of gifts, dolls in a glass case, bins of sweets with price cards at the front, and boxed figurines stacked by the door.

JEAN NICOLE.note: Jean Nicole (from the photos): a rust-red fascia with the name in fat white brush script, a yellow dot over the i; a mirrored soffit, a red shop on red carpet: round racks of pastel blouses, maroon sale cards in chrome frames on stands, forms in pastel suits up on the fixtures.

LADY FOOT LOCKER.note: Lady Foot Locker (from the photo): a white canopy fascia with round green lettering, glass bays on white tile either side with big posters, and an open front on cream slatwall: tees along the top, red LFL squares, the shoe wall, a form in a neon tee, a green door, red SALE boards.

MILLER'S OUTPOST.note: Miller's Outpost (from the photos): a pale grey front with a red line framing the wide opening, heavy red serif capitals standing off on black returns, a round white badge with the red-and-gold M at each end; a bright open shop: timber wall fixtures of tees and denim, the big band poster, tables of folded shirts, torso forms in red and pink, blue price boards on stands either side, red clearance cards and star-striped balloons.

MASTERCUTS.note: MasterCuts (from the photos): a band of sea-green terrazzo with two brass lines, white condensed lettering standing off on black returns, a fluted cherry rail and cherry piers; shelves of bottles, a style poster, price balloons.

FATHER & SON.note: Father & Son Shoes (from the photo): a deep walnut fascia with white slanted slab capitals, downlights under it, brown columns; glowing cream walls lined with shelf on shelf of men's shoes, the name again in small letters on each wall, round tables in rust skirts, tan tub chairs, rust carpet.

FOOTACTION USA.note: Footaction USA (from the photos): a grey sign beam on dark steel posts, wide white capitals with a bar under them and USA in blue, a big outlined star glowing blue at the end; inside, lit shoe walls, hung jerseys, torso forms in red and white over tables of trainers, a floor of black tile set with logo squares.

LION'S SHARE RESTAURANT.note: Lion's Share: a dark brown brick front with no windows, a carved plaque with the name in gold, two coach lamps, and a single open doorway onto a dim passage that leads back to the dining room.

SOLARIUM.note: Solarium (from the owner's memory of it): a pale stone fascia carrying only the name, in soft aqua-green lowercase neon bent as one tight line; under it a glass front onto a calm tanning-salon lobby: sea-glass walls, a white front desk with an aqua stripe, a palm, a shelf of lotions and a lit beach print.

CONCEPTS.note: Concepts: school uniforms and backpacks for kids. Instead of windows, two deep white shadow boxes either side of the door, each holding huge plain geometric solids about the height of a three-year-old: a sphere, a cone, a cube, a cylinder (the colours are a guess until a photo turns up). Through the door, racks of navy and white uniforms, plaid jumpers, khakis and a wall of backpacks.

COUNTRY FAIR.note: Country Fair (from descriptions only, not yet a photo): a green fascia with the name in cream serif, a white picket fence running across the front under the windows, and a shop full of country gifts: a quilt, baskets, candles, wooden hearts and dried flowers, with a gingham valance over the door.

KARMELKORN.note: Karmelkorn (from the photo): a golden-yellow bulkhead wrapping the corner with the red logotype drawn by hand (the big swash K, then slab-serif capitals, red with a cream edge and a deep red shadow, leaning a little), a lit soffit, and an open counter: glass cases of tins and bagged corn on a black boarded base under a blue-black top, yellow walls, the steel hood and popper, shelves of tins. The corner is open: nothing here draws a post, the bulkhead, soffit, counter and base all run to the very edge of each face so they meet cleanly round the angle.

GUMBALLS.note: Gumballs (from the owner's memory and two photographs): a white fascia with GUMBALLS in red and a little gumball machine beside the word, the same on both faces of the corner; under it the front is wide open between square white piers. Inside: a white candy kiosk with a glass case of bulk candy up front and gumball machines on the floor; tall white shelving of toys, Looney Tunes plush and Beanie Babies along the sides; a black round display tower in the middle; and at the back the dark black-light corner: glowing posters, lava lamps, a plasma ball and bead curtains.

ZALES.note: Zales, from a photograph of the shop: stone-tile piers and header, a wood fascia carrying a mauve sign box with brushed-silver letters, and an open front onto lit glass jewellery cases on a wood base, a cream room with a square column, recessed ceiling lights and the shop's own plaque on the back wall. The logo is drawn by hand as outlines: the wide Z, the A as two legs over a cut diamond, the E with a wedge for its middle arm, the angular S.

GORDON'S JEWELERS.note: Gordon's Jewelers, from photographs of the shop: a dark bronze header holding a row of back-lit frosted panels crossed by one long arch, the name on the centre panel; under it an open front onto a dim taupe room hung with framed pictures under track lights, and lit glass cases on a dark mahogany base. The name is drawn by hand as outlines in the sign's narrow, high-contrast serif: thick sides and hairline tops to the round letters, flat serifs.

GRYDER'S.note: Gryder's Shoes, from a photograph: a dark ribbed-wood fascia with white slab-serif letters (traced from the photo), an open front under fluorescent panels and track lights, ficus trees and a T-shirt rack to the left, shoes on white cube pedestals and lit wall shelves, quarry-tile floor

BAKERS.note: Bakers, from photographs: a white back-lit sign box with thin navy capitals standing on its ledge, cherry-wood columns either side of the entry, and tall glass windows onto cream display steps of shoes, boots and bags

AMERICAN BANK.note: American Bank, from a grainy photograph of the Southland Mall branch: a white stucco front, the name in heavy rounded white letters on the shaded wall above, one wide arch closed by a wrought-iron gate, and a black carriage lantern on each side. The photograph is black and white, so the colours are a guess.

GOLDEN CHAIN GANG.note: Golden Chain Gang: the shop's own mark, traced from its 1994 newspaper advertisement (three big outlined G's down the left, GOLDEN / CHAIN / GANG beside them, a chain running down to a ball), painted in gold on a black front; below it an open counter of lit cases and chains on display busts. Colours are a guess: the ad is black and white.

CORN DOG 7.note: Corn Dog 7, from a photograph of the Southland Mall shop: a glowing yellow sign box with the name in fat black brush italics and "seasoned fries" / "fresh lemonade" on a navy rule (all traced from the photo); navy-and-yellow tile piers; inside, a dark-wood dining room with booths on the left and, on the right, the counter: navy tile with yellow panels of black checks, glass food cases under a steel hood, blue menu boards; herringbone brick floor. Drawn flat and straight-on, as vector art.

CLAIRE'S BOUTIQUES.note: Claire's, after a photograph of a 1990s shop: a wall of pink-veined cream marble, a white sign box with the name in tall narrow dark-red letters lit red from behind and ACCESSORIES in spaced capitals, and a wide opening under a dark soffit onto walls of carded jewellery, bags, hats and sale signs. The name is drawn by hand as outlines. Flat vector art.

CUCOS BORDER CAFE.note: Cucos Mexican Cafe, after photographs: a front of warm vertical wood planks with teal-green trim and a stepped parapet; the sign board with pale peach stripes behind the big red swash logo (traced from a photo of the sign, with its dark drop shadow) and MEXICAN CAFE beneath; heavy wood lintels over dark double doors; and a clay-tile awning on a green fascia over white-mullioned windows each side. Flat vector art.

BABBAGE'S.note: Babbage's, the video game shop, after photographs: a white curved bulkhead with the name in fat rounded pink neon letters (drawn by hand, stroke by stroke), a dark red column each side of a wide opening, and a bright shop of game boxes on slatwall, a poster rack, a counter and a stack of boxed consoles. Flat vector art.

POCKET CHANGE.note: Pocket Change (from the photo of the Southland store): pale blue gloss tile stepping down the mall wall either side, glass-block columns, raised silver capitals, and a dark room of lit crane machines

K&B.note: K&B: tan board-and-batten fascia, and the purple oval with its gold rim and fat white K&B

WOOLWORTH.note: Woolworth: red panel fascia, a white light-box with red slab-serif lettering shadowed in gold, and a wide open front onto a bright white five-and-dime: yellow wall bands, red aisle signs, gondolas, red carts || F.W. Woolworth, rebuilt from photographs. Two fronts in one: the variety store, and at its right-hand end the Coffee Shop. Store: a pale panelled fascia carrying WOOLWORTH in the mall's own fat slab-serif letters (drawn by hand as outlines after the photograph of the Southland sign) lit as red neon; a show window, a wide open entrance and a second window, looking down the aisles of a bright sales floor. Coffee Shop: beige wall with COFFEE SHOP in wide red capitals over a grey band and a red stripe; one door-width opening, then glass onto the booths and the lunch counter, whose short end stands near the front at the far right and whose long side runs away toward the back. Everything below is drawn as vector art in simple one-point perspective, so it stays sharp at any size.

SOUND SHOP.note: Sound Shop: a plain taupe bulkhead carrying fat rounded italic letters lit yellow to orange with a red halo, over a satin-aluminium door frame and one big sheet of glass onto the record bins

LANE BRYANT.note: Lane Bryant: a warm wood portal with a black sign band and thin white capitals, frameless glass bays either side under a cream soffit, and a bright cream shop with a wood floor

RAVE.note: Rave: stacked, offset brushed-silver plates stepping out from the bulkhead, the white sign plate proud of them with heavy pink-red italics sliced by a speed line; under it a dim shop of posters and black clothes

TEE TAI'S.note: Tee Tai's: a black sign box with the name in pale gold brush script (long sweeping bars on the two T's), a black fretwork rail under it, and red paper lanterns with gold bands and tassels hung along the front

SOUTHLAND CINEMA.note: Southland Cinema, from the photograph: the wing's brick wall carried right across the front; in the middle a tall arched entrance in a white frame, its half-round head filled with a dark red-brown mosaic, a little chandelier hanging in it and the cinema's roundel at the crown; under the transom a glass wall of three bays, double doors in the middle, looking into the dark lobby and its concession counter; a lit poster case set into the brick either side (Jurassic Park and The Firm on the left, Last Action Hero and another on the right), and a black coach lantern glowing on the wall above each case.

JCPENNEY.note: JCPenney as it looked in the mall: diagonal wood plank fascia, white letters, dark columns, wide open front

DILLARD'S.note: Dillard's: polished brown stone fascia, white back-lit serif letters, a cream soffit, and a wide open front onto a floor with a bright ceiling tray, dark wood columns and tan tile
